stories.title: Active Window Management
stories.summary: Implemented active window management module to enforce learning efficiency constraints. The 8-word active limit prevents cognitive overload, while the 4-new-per-batch cap ensures learners focus on core vocabulary before expanding. Words in the `srsM2_review` phase are identified as "active" — a natural entry point after mastery is demonstrated. **Key Implementation**: - Extended `WordState` type with `batchesSinceLastProgress?` and `shelvedUntil?` fields (for EP05-ST02 dependency) - Created `getEligibleWords()` function: identifies active words, calculates available new-word slots, filters eligible candidates - Comprehensive unit tests: 20 tests covering boundary cases (0–8 active, slot math, filtering, immutability, edge configs)

stories.title: Stuck Word Detection + Shelving
stories.summary: Implemented stuck word detection and shelving system for the SRS engine. Words that show no mastery progress for 3 consecutive batches are marked as "stuck" and shelved for 1 day to allow cognitive reset. System respects a max-2 shelved cap, with overflow logic (newest stuck word is shelved when capacity is reached). All functions are immutable and time-aware.

Added E2E integration test: seed → batch → answers (all correct) → assert `processed` count and `masteryCount > 0` for each updated word. stories.title: Mixed Question Direction for `/api/srs/batch`
stories.summary: `POST /api/srs/batch` now assigns a random direction to each `multiple_choice` question — either `english_to_native` (see English sound, pick Thai char) or `native_to_english` (see Thai char, pick English sound). The direction is exposed in the wire response as `questionDirection` so the client can render the prompt correctly. The `buildMcChoices` helper was refactored to accept a `direction` parameter and derive `targetText`, `correctText`, and distractor field from it.

stories.title: Add `native_to_romanization` Question Direction
stories.summary: Added a third MC question direction: `native_to_romanization` (see Thai character, pick the consonant's full romanization name). This tests a distinct skill from `native_to_english` — many consonants share the same English sound (`"kh"` maps to ข, ค, ฆ, ฅ), making romanization the only unambiguous label. The direction picker was changed from a 50/50 coin flip to a uniform 1-of-3 selection via a `DIRECTIONS` constant array.

stories.summary: Renamed the shared quiz-question type to be explicit that it's a multiple-choice question, then introduced a broader question type that can represent either a multiple-choice question or a future sentence question — clearing the way for a sentence composer to plug into the same type family.

stories.title: EP23-DS02
stories.summary: Designed and delivered a sentence-level composer that turns a pre-written sentence into three "arrange the tiles in order" question types — from an English prompt, from a romanized prompt, and from a native-script prompt — and wired each one into the terminal runner as it was built, story by story, so it could be tried out immediately. Introduced an eligibility rule so these sentence questions only appear once every word in the sentence has been seen enough times.

stories.title: EP23-ST03
stories.summary: Defined the shape of a pre-written sentence record and added two sample Thai sentences built from real vocabulary, plus a small per-language config describing how words join into a displayed sentence (with vs. without spaces between words).

stories.title: EP23-ST04
stories.summary: Built the first "arrange the tiles in order" sentence question — reconstructing native word order from an English prompt — and wired it into the terminal runner so a learner only sees it once every word in the sentence has been seen enough times, with a numbered-tile answer input and a cheat-sheet hint line.

stories.title: EP23-ST05
stories.summary: Added a second sentence-question direction — reconstructing native word order starting from a romanized prompt instead of English — reusing the same composer and runner wiring from ST04 with no extra plumbing needed.

stories.title: EP23-ST06
stories.summary: Added a third sentence-question direction — reconstructing the romanized word order starting from a native-script prompt — completing the full set of three directions the sentence composer supports.

stories.title: EP23-ST07
stories.summary: Added an end-to-end test confirming all three sentence-question directions come back in a fixed order, share the same sentence identity, and share the same correct word order, and confirmed the whole package type-checks cleanly with the new sentence composer wired in.

stories.title: EP23-BUG01
stories.summary: Added a safety-net check that inspects a finished quiz batch and flags two kinds of problems: a word that should have been excluded sneaking back in (either as its own question or hidden inside a sentence's word tiles), and the same question appearing twice in one batch. The check only reports problems — it never fixes or blocks anything itself; callers decide what to do with a flagged batch.

stories.title: EP20-ST02
stories.summary: Set up the package so it runs from the workspace root and added a smoke test confirming the mock data loads.

stories.title: EP20-ST03
stories.summary: Built the first working quiz: for one consonant, generates four multiple-choice questions (one per direction) and runs them interactively in the terminal with feedback and a score.

stories.title: EP20-ST04
stories.summary: Extended quizzing to multiple words at once with a configurable question limit, guaranteeing every word appears at least once, and made the terminal runner accept single keypresses instead of requiring Enter.

stories.title: EP20-ST05
stories.summary: Added support for quizzing on regular vocabulary words alongside consonants by introducing a shared quiz-item type, while keeping distractor pools separate per item type.

stories.title: EP20-ST06
stories.summary: Introduced formal "deck" and "batch" concepts — a deck holds word and foundational-content pools, and batches are fixed-size slices run one after another with a summary at the end.

stories.title: EP20-ST07
stories.summary: Added tracking of how many times each word has been seen and answered correctly across a run, shown as a per-word summary after each batch.

stories.title: EP20-ST08
stories.summary: Replaced the fixed batch sequence with an adaptive loop: words cycle through queued → active → mastered, and the session automatically continues until everything is mastered.

stories.title: EP20-ST09
stories.summary: Replaced the simple correct-count mastery rule with a streak-based system — consecutive right or wrong answers raise or lower a 0–5 mastery level, with fast climbs/drops once a streak passes threshold.

stories.title: EP20-ST11
stories.summary: Added a one-time "re-check" for words that were already mastered when a new deck loads — a correct answer confirms mastery, a wrong answer returns the word to active play without resetting its streak history.

stories.title: EP20-DS01
stories.summary: Design spec for a code-quality cleanup of the interactive runner: splitting an oversized function, removing cryptic variable names, removing duplicated input-handling code, and adding input validation. No behavior change intended.

stories.title: EP20-ST12
stories.summary: Delivered the DS01 cleanup: broke the run loop into smaller functions, renamed unclear variables, consolidated duplicated input-reading code, and added validation with clearer error messages. Confirmed zero behavior change (all 83 tests pass).

stories.title: EP20-ST13
stories.summary: Added full support for Thai vowels and tones alongside consonants, using an explicit type tag instead of guessing content type from field shape. Tones were limited to 2 quiz directions (instead of 4) because distinguishing tiny diacritic marks visually was too hard; a placeholder character was added so standalone marks render legibly in the terminal.
